reaction_equations: A W-SiHyF* z 1 WF6(g)! W-WF* x 1 SiHaFb(g) (1)
B WF* x 1 Si2H6(g)! W-SiHyF* z 1 2H2(g) 1 SiHaFb(g) (2)
surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the sequential exposure of WF6 and Si2H6 in an ABAB sequence. The Si2H6 reactant serves a sacrificial role to strip fluorine from tungsten without incorporating into the film. The WF6 half-reaction proceeds to completion, producing W-WF* species, while the Si2H6 half-reaction generates SiHyF* species. These species are then removed in subsequent cycles, ensuring self-limiting surface chemistry.
evidence: The text describes the surface reactions as follows: 'A W-SiHyF* z 1 WF6(g)! W-WF* x 1 SiHaFb(g) (1)' and 'B WF* x 1 Si2H6(g)! W-SiHyF* z 1 2H2(g) 1 SiHaFb(g) (2)'. It also states, 'The Si2H6 reactant serves a sacrificial role to strip fluorine from tungsten without incorporating into the film.'
